title: Kingdom of Numbers
subtitle: Look, those numbers are no longer curled up on the manuscript.

content.text: You still look confused … I know, darling, you haven't even vomited up the mouthfuls of sea water you ingested deep into your stomach. Just relax and lie where you are! You don't have to get back on your feet right away.
Usually, yes, usually, when those drunkards and patients wake up from a coma, just like you do right now, they only have two questions.
The first one will help you find out the name of the land you are lying on.
And the other will help you calibrate that bizarre watch on your wrist.
Alright, now it's finally the right time to make things clear. Open your mouth and throw up whatever you have, sea water, questions ... Just get them all out, right here.

branch.text: Oh, darling, it's an honor to be your first question and the one haunting your mind.

But I'm going to let you down, I'm afraid. I don't have any breathtaking stories to tell, just one simple fact after another. You know, the most popular topic among women my age is the healthy oatmeal our teeth can barely handle.

Luckily, my ears are more reliable than my teeth. I can still nag like I always do, answer questions to my knowledge, and have a little chit chat with you sometimes. So, to summarize it, just consider me a kindhearted chatterbox.

content.text: Where's the guy who used to talk to me?

branch.text: Oh darling, why not let it be? You're all on your own now. Don't ask for more when you already have someone to talk to, even if I'm only nagging most of the time.
We gotta let the past be the past, like how we deal with old newspapers, because all I speak is one simple fact after another.
Anyways, we will keep each other company for quite a while.
Finally, a question about yourself. In front of you is a boundless sea. All you can see, besides the beach you are lying on, is water, water, and water ...
A cry for help will be drowned out by the waves, and even the strongest legs are tied to the ground here and cannot break free.

See? There's no way to leave, but it's a good opportunity to have an island tour. The locals have good manners, so I think you can ask them to show you around. That's at least better than just goofing off.

content.text: What time is it now exactly?

branch.text: Not even you can avoid asking this question. But a kindhearted soul already told you that time is moving forward as it used to be, step by step. So, the time is ... the year 2007.
Yes, time is back on the right track, going where it's supposed to be. Raindrops literally drop again, and no one goes back to the past anymore ... Well, some miss the good old days, though.

Oh ... You still doubt it, don't you? I can see it in your eyes. Don't get me wrong, I'm on your side. After all the hard times I have experienced, if anyone told me that my life was just a boring dream, one neither good nor bad, I would throw a shoe at them!
I can tell you are being burned by anxiety. But to find the "time" you want, we need to comb through the situation, like how you do with your hair.
Time is like a Sachertorte, and now it has been divided into many pieces. On the largest piece stands the white chocolate card—yes, the last good days of the 20th century.

The gentlemen are still growing handlebar mustaches, and the ladies have not yet flattened the curves on their bodies. New money buys one art piece after another to show off their good taste. They don't even mind turning their homes into museums.
A cafe named San Marco officially opens, gathering the most outstanding intellectuals and writers of the time. They talk and laugh there, as if nothing could stand in their way.
Then the cafe receives a neurologist whose briefcase carries the interpretation of dreams, and celluloid film and projectors become a new means of expression for artists.
At this point, helmets remain intact in the warehouse, gauze only works in hospitals, bullets only fly in the firing range, and the flame that swallows lives is not even lit ...
But soon, soon enough ... the young people who swore to retrieve their homeland will take up daggers and guns to fulfill their oath.

Buildings will shake like a leaf, and rocks will fall off and hit the walls. Screams will try to break free from people's throats. At that moment, a clip will be loaded secretly, in the name of supreme honor.
A golden age is about to end. A vortex of blood is already swirling in the river of time, waiting to devour everything that passes by.

When that actually happens, all the beautiful curves derived from nature, the bee-shaped brooches, the punch, the eiderdown duvets, everything will be destroyed, leaving only an insurance contract behind, and it doesn't even work.
Even this cafe will be smashed into concrete pieces.
See? We have combed the hair now. Everything I just talked about is the "time" you want.

Heh heh, you wouldn't buy the nonsense about the fairness of time when you reach my age.
It actually feels different between those who keep their eyes shut and those who keep theirs open; likewise, those who kill never share the same feeling with those who are killed; this is also true between those who have enough food to eat and those who are starving ...
Alright, that's it. I've talked enough. Now get up, darling, and brush the sand off yourself. Trust me, you will find your own answer to this era.

trails.title: Trail② The Third Party in Confrontation
trails.description: Dolphins, curious about terrestrial creatures' communication, try to join the confrontation.

items.text: Kingdom of Numbers

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You are saying we are in 2007?
The heart is pounding fast in the chest.
Perhaps it's the only chance.
She nods her head.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you know the "Storm"?
Is that how you call it?
We call it the Emanation.
The tide of pneuma is pouring down from above and converging. It would raise as a tsunami and break the world of Matters where darkness abounds.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I don't understand.
She tilts her head and seems equally confused.
This shouldn't be hard for you to understand. You are also a real number.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I am 37. What's your number?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm Vertin.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: No, no. I'm asking your number.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: The scripture says, only the people who are still in search of their essences would identify themselves by a combination of meaningless phonetic symbols.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Hmm, well, so you don't know your number yet, just like Sophia.
None of her words make any sense.
But this is not the most urgent matter one needs to worry about.
Sonetto, Regulus, Lilya, Ms. Radio, and the Razor Squad ... where are they?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Have you seen my companions?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Yes!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Are you looking for the integer or the fraction? Or the irrational number? Or the imaginary number?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Integers are the living example of virtues. Fractions can be understood through specific means. Irrational numbers are the free spirits, while imaginary numbers are the existence which doesn't belong to this dimension of the number axis.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Which one are you looking for?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll ask something else instead. What is this place?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Island.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What island?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Have you seen another island?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Huh! Maybe another question.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Did a biographer named Urd visit here before, in 1999?
That takes her a while to think about.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: 1999 is a lovely centered triangular number, but I believe this number has been abused in the doomsday stories. I mean, people are too invested in its meaning. In fact, 1999 is nothing special compared to 1991 and 1993 …

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: However, 999 is a brilliant number! It is a Kaprekar number, a Palindromic number, and the largest three-digit natural number ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sorry to interrupt, but I only meant to ask about Urd, the biographer. She had been here on this island and written a travel note called Roaming in Apeiron.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Does the name or the book ring a bell?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I am sorry.
Once again, she shakes her head.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: I have no idea about the fragments of Matters you are talking about.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Fragments of ... Matters?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Help! Somebody help!
A scream comes from behind.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: *coughs* Captain, you should go. This APPLe's arm has ...

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: No, Mr. APPLe, stay with me for a little longer!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Piss off! Shush! You wicked dolphins! Mr. APPLe is not your breakfast, nor are my records!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Huh, isn't that Vertin?!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Vertin! Are you done with the standing and staring?! Come give us a hand!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Phew, thank God you are here, Vertin! Mr. APPLe and I were this close to being made a Stargazy pie by these clever bastards and served to the dinner table!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You've also been incredibly helpful, Regulus.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Is that so? Like how?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You rebuilt my confidence in communicating with people.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Have you seen Sonetto and the others?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: No. I woke up on a dolphin's back.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Thought they had saved my life at first, I was quite grateful to them. But the next moment, they just started all the beating and biting!

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: They think you are an irrational number. That's why they bit you!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Whoa, this little lady made me jump! Vertin, who is this long-haired stranger?
A familiar voice calls from the distance.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Thank goodness. You are all safe and sound!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Lilya is on her way. Now we only need to find the captain and his team members ...
Next to her stand several strangers in white garments.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, these people are ...?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: They are the Apeiron believers. They lent us a helping hand after the ship went down.
The robed figures stand unspeaking and motionless.
Until one steps forward to break the silence.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Not at all. An integer is under an obligation to help his kind.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Ms. Sonetto, have you found your friends?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Yes, only the members of the Razor Squad are still missing. They also belong to the St. Pavlov Foundation, like we do.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Imaginary numbers are not of our concern.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Imaginary numbers?

items.speaker: Six
items.text: You should not linger here if you've already found your lost friends. We will provide a boat for you to leave.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Our school of thought does not accommodate uninvited guests.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Wait, we have something to ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What if we know about the Emanation?
The man halts.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We are the investigators from St. Pavlov Foundation. We are glad to share the information about the "Storm" or the Emanation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please grant us entry to this island so that we can share them.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll explain to you later. Trust me, please, Sonetto.
The white robes whisper to each other.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Come this way. We will talk.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: However, only integers and fractions are welcomed here.
The man puts out a finger, directly pointing at Regulus.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: No irrational number is allowed on this island.

items.speaker: Six
items.text: Throw her into the sea!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Huh?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Wait, now hold on a second! I said hol- …
TO BE CONTINUED…
